_meta.purpose: Real, publicly-sourced platforms and systems per archetype. Generators inject the relevant slice into prompts; validate_process() logs any system a page names that is not here.
_meta.rule: Only names with public sourcing appear here. Where a layer is genuinely undocumented it is recorded as a sparse_layer with evidence_gap text instead of an invented product name.

drone-delivery.name: FAA Part 108 (PROPOSED — NOT IN FORCE)
drone-delivery.capability: Proposed BVLOS rule replacing the Part 107 waiver system. Covers operations up to 1,320 lb with two approval levels (Permitted Operations, Operational Certificate) and five risk categories by population density
drone-delivery.status_caveat: NPRM ONLY as of 29 Aug 2026. Published 7 Aug 2025; comments closed 6 Oct 2025 with 3,000+ responses; reopened 28 Jan - 11 Feb 2026 for right-of-way and electronic conspicuity. Held in OIRA review since 10 Jul 2026. Final rule likely late 2026 into 2027. NO operator can claim Part 108 authority today.

sparse_layers.layer: Production AV software stack (perception, prediction, planning, control)
sparse_layers.evidence_gap: Waymo does not publish component names or architecture for its production driving stack. Only simulation and test infrastructure is publicly named.
Waymo confirms remote assistance exists as a capability but publishes no product name, interface design or operator-to-vehicle ratio.
No eVTOL operator has entered commercial service, so no operational software estate is documented.
Vertiport operations exist as FAA concept-of-operations text, not as documented deployed systems.
Wisk's ground-supervision concept of operations, supervisor-to-aircraft ratio and tooling are not published.
Zipline, Wing and Prime Air publish aircraft and network facts but not internal dispatch/orchestration product names.
